question: Let $k,n,r$ be positive integers. (a) Let $Q(x)=x^k+a_1x^{k+1}+\cdots+a_nx^{k+n}$ be a polynomial with real coefficients. Show that the function $\frac{Q(x)}{x^k}$ is strictly positive for all real $x$ satisfying $0<|x|<\frac{1}{1+\sum_{i=1}^n|a_i|}$. (b) Let $P(x)=b_0+b_1x+\cdots+b_rx^r$ be a non-zero polynomial with real coefficients. Let $m$ be the smallest number such that $b_m\ne0$. Prove that the graph of $y=P(x)$ cuts the $x$-axis at the origin (i.e. $P$ changes sign at $x=0$) if and only if $m$ is an odd integer.
